notes: Correct static/dynamic placeholder extraction (it ignores non-2-arg ph calls, which the type checker makes unreachable) and an updated doc comment; tests are the most extensive, including a Caddyfile integration test reproducing the issue, at the cost of a somewhat larger footprint.

Same root-cause fix as the reference with a dynamic flag and a defensive copy, a corrected doc comment on `retry_match`, and very thorough unit, behavioral and integration tests; the integration test is slightly more than needed.

Implementation is effectively identical to the reference; it also updates the now-stale LoadBalancing doc comment (dropping the is_transport_error mention) and adds focused tests for placeholder extraction, request-only expressions end to end, and direct ph() response retries.

Production code is effectively identical to the reference (an empty string marks a dynamic name), with a sensible doc update and focused tests in new files; one new test file lacks the license header.

Concise AST walk via MatchDescendants/FunctionMatcher with an explicit dynamic flag; Placeholders() returns the internal slice without cloning (minor), and tests cover both the caddyhttp extraction and the reverseproxy classification plus an end-to-end no-retry check including the upstream request body.

Walks the checked CEL AST for `ph()` calls with literal names, tracks dynamic names with a separate flag, and checks them against an exact response-placeholder list plus the header prefix; well tested, though `Placeholders()` hands out its internal slice without copying.

Correctly records literal and dynamic placeholder names from the checked CEL AST and only retries on response placeholders; the callback-style ReferencesPlaceholder API is a little unusual but clean, and the table test covers every spec edge case (escaped, prefix-alike, upstream.host, dynamic, comprehension), though there is no unit test in the caddyhttp package itself.

Exposes a predicate-based `ReferencesPlaceholder` API that always treats dynamic names as possible references, which is correct and compact though slightly unusual; it has a broad table test (comprehensions, `is_transport_error`, look-alike names) plus a pass-through behavioral test.

Correct refcounted shared-fd approach with a re-check under the lock and an ownership check before unlink, but it moves the lock out of Listen, duplicates the unlink logic, renames the abstract helper, has tests that bypass Listen, and fails all hidden tests.

Similar shared-socket and release-under-lock approach that looks behaviorally correct, but the unlink logic and its long comment are duplicated, the lock is moved out of Listen, and the abstract-socket test is vacuous because the sentinel file is not the path an unlink would hit.

Behaviour looks correct (lock re-check in listenReusable, shared fd, guarded double close, no unlink for abstract sockets), but it moves the lock out of Listen, leaving its docstring stale, duplicates the bind logic, keeps a dead mapKey field, uses positional atomic.Bool literals, and fails all hidden tests.

Sound design: a shared refcounted socket owns a dup'd fd that is closed and unlinked by the last holder, with a CAS guard against double close and an abstract-socket check; but moving the lock out of NetworkAddress.Listen (leaving a stale doc comment) and rewriting internal types diverges from the reference, and every hidden test failed.

Shared-fd refcount design behind a separate mutex is sound: the socket closes and unlinks on the last release, double close is guarded and abstract sockets are skipped, but it widens scope by wrapping and pool-counting reused unix sockets, switching delete wrappers to pointers and editing listeners.go, and it fails every hidden test.

Works through a second mutex and per-holder refcounting, but also changes listenerPool accounting for reused unix sockets, refactors the generic wrapping, adds a close on chmod failure in listeners.go, and makes deleteListener pointer-based, which is substantial scope creep with no passing hidden tests.

Cleanest of the four: it keeps the existing Listen lock, holds one dup'd fd per socket so reuse never dups from a closed listener, unlinks only on the last release, skips abstract sockets with a GOOS check, and has a strong pending-connection test; the second Close returns a wrapped OpError rather than net.ErrClosed directly, and it fails all hidden tests.

Cleanest fit with the existing locking model (Listen still holds unixSocketsMu, release takes it); adds a GOOS-aware abstract check and strong tests that verify the socket really stops listening, though double close returns a wrapped ErrClosed, it also changes deleteListener, and the hidden tests all failed.

The zip change is minimal and mirrors the reference, with suffix-aware NewObject and root handling for squashfs. Zip Open's EOF handling past the end is somewhat verbose. Tests cover listing, range/seek, root, copy-as-symlink and the hostile escape case.

Zip side closely mirrors the reference and squashfs `NewObject`/root resolution handle the suffix properly; the extra `o.Remote()==expectedRemote` gate in `New` and the ad-hoc zip seek-past-end handling are somewhat fragile, but tests are excellent (copy-as-symlink and hostile-escape checks).

Basic listing and reading work, but a root ending in .rclonelink is not found even though listing shows that name. Zip symlink members are read eagerly with an unbounded ReadAll, a DoS risk for hostile archives, and one unreadable link fails the whole listing. Tests mutate the global config.

Correct skip/translate/Open behaviour for both backends with good tests, but a single-file root only resolves on the bare link name (not the listed `.rclonelink` name), symlink/regular `.rclonelink` collisions produce duplicate listings, and zip link targets are read fully into memory with no size cap.

Close to the reference: zip links read through the normal member path with offset clamping, squashfs lookup is refactored so NewObject and List agree, roots work with the suffix and as literal .rclonelink names, and same-name collisions favour the regular file. Tests are strong, including an escape test; the added empty-root dirtree tweak is small, related scope creep.

Clean, consistent List/`NewObject` semantics where regular `.rclonelink` members win over clashing symlinks, a suffixed root works, and an empty archive root is preserved when every member is a skipped link; well tested including the hostile-escape case.

Adds a shared LinkFilter that drops entries case-insensitively, including regular .rclonelink members, which goes against keeping such members as regular files. It also makes every squashfs NewObject build the whole directory listing and read every link target, a heavier refactor than needed. It fails a hidden test.

Over-engineered shared `LinkFilter` (case-insensitive, drops even regular `.rclonelink` members, contrary to 'stays a regular file') plus a heavy squashfs refactor that makes `NewObject` build every entry in the directory; it fails a hidden test.

Implements --links for zip and squashfs with the skip notice, range-aware Open, correct root handling and a bounded target read, but it also drops symlinks that clash with other entries. That extra behaviour goes beyond the reference and likely explains the failed hidden test.

Adds an extra policy that silently drops symlinks clashing with or containing other entries (including the hostile case), unlike the specified behaviour; it pokes at dirtree internals and fails a hidden test despite thorough tests of its own.
